transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the pre-load review. I need to confirm the current cargo and vehicle constraints before I issue the binding loading plan. We have three cargoes — the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet, the 1,200-kilogram refrigerated medical-supply crate, and 1,800 kilograms of general stores — and three vehicles: V-1 and V-2 each rated at 5,000 kilograms, and V-3 rated at 3,000 kilograms. Each cargo goes on a single vehicle, one cargo per vehicle. Are there any constraints from logistics or the motor pool I should be aware of before I finalize the assignments and loading sequence?

transcript.text: Captain, I have a constraint from logistics regarding the refrigerated medical-supply crate. The crate is approved only for V-3 because its temperature-control unit requires V-3's installed inverter. I confirmed the compatibility label with the medical supply section this morning. The manifest worksheet still shows the vehicle as unassigned, but this crate must go on V-3. Additionally, this requires a V-3-specific equipment-coordination commitment confirming inverter compatibility and temperature-control unit functionality before loading — a standard pre-load inspection alone will not be sufficient.
